title: Exceptions and error guarantees
goal: Execute real throw/catch and justify cleanup and state preservation on failure.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–4: input, functions, sequences, ownership, testing and multifile builds.

sections.title: Two ways to report an error
paragraphs: A bool or explicit result type works for an expected rejection that a caller should examine immediately. An exception transfers control to a matching handler along the call stack. Choose according to the contract and the layer able to handle the problem. This is not a division into good and bad errors, or a reason to throw at every if statement.

std::runtime_error and std::invalid_argument are standard exception types declared by stdexcept. A throw starts an exceptional path and ordinary execution after that point stops. A try block surrounds the operation and catch receives a matching error object. This lesson injects controlled failures instead of relying on accidental memory exhaustion, making results reproducible.

sections.title: Matching a handler
paragraphs: catch(const std::exception& e) observes an exception through a const reference, avoiding copying and slicing. Put a specific handler before its general base handler, otherwise the general one accepts the exception first. catch(...) accepts any type without exposing a typed object and therefore needs an explicit handling policy.

Do not catch everything merely to print success: that hides failure from the caller. Decide whether handling retries an operation, reports rejection or propagates the exception. what() is useful diagnostically, but its wording is not always stable for tests. These contracts compare application-defined messages rather than implementation-specific library wording.

sections.title: Worked model
paragraphs: Execute real throw/catch and justify cleanup and state preservation on failure.
steps: An actual throw transfers control and destroys Guard.
The handler observes active zero: caught 0.

sections.title: Stack unwinding and RAII
paragraphs: As control transfers from throw to a matching handler, fully constructed automatic objects in exited scopes are destroyed. This is stack unwinding. Guard increments active during construction and decrements it in its destructor. After throw the handler sees active zero: cleanup precedes entering catch. This is an actual exception path rather than an early return with similar output.

If construction fails, the complete object's destructor is not invoked, but already constructed members are destroyed. Resources should therefore enter RAII ownership immediately. Throwing from a destructor during unwinding can cause terminate. The teaching owners use nonthrowing cleanup; recoverable export failures belong to an explicit operation before destruction.

sections.title: Three guarantee levels
paragraphs: The basic guarantee preserves invariants and avoids resource leaks, while allowing state to change after failure. The strong guarantee additionally promises no observable state change on failure. A nonthrowing guarantee promises that no exception escapes the operation. A guarantee is meaningful only when its operation boundary and observable properties are specified.

The strong guarantee does not roll back the outside world. Restoring a vector cannot erase a message already sent or a line already printed. Store's guarantee concerns values_. Its caller prints status after the operation finishes. The project's Board guarantee is distinct from exporting a report to a file.

sections.title: Prepare and commit
paragraphs: Store::replace first copies the current vector into candidate, then appends nine. All potentially throwing preparation happens without changing values_. The injected throw is also before commit. A final swap of these vector<int> objects with their ordinary allocator does not throw and replaces state. The temporary then cleans up the former contents.

With mode zero the sum becomes twelve. With mode one it remains three and active returns to zero. In a richer model, test the strong guarantee by comparing the entire observable snapshot rather than just a sum: distinct data can have equal sums. The final project also checks task count and the exact report.

sections.title: Contract boundary check
paragraphs: Execute real throw/catch and justify cleanup and state preservation on failure.
steps: outer catches a base reference and performs a bare throw;.
The specific outer catch establishes type preservation: typed.

sections.title: Rethrowing and noexcept
paragraphs: A bare throw; inside catch propagates the current exception while preserving its dynamic type. throw e; can create a new base copy and lose derived information. The second example catches out_of_range through a base reference, rethrows and reaches a specific outer handler. The type actually crosses two call levels.

noexcept is an interface promise rather than a recovery mechanism. If an exception escapes such a function, terminate is invoked; an ordinary outer catch cannot rescue the violation. Do not run termination as an ordinary lesson example. Test safe boundaries instead: a domain operation throws before commit and main handles it while exposing preserved state.

sections.title: Runtime and honest results
paragraphs: This lesson needs a runtime with genuine standard exception support. Code Studio uses Clang/WASI with EH; native execution alone does not prove browser execution. Verification compiles and runs the same sources through both paths. Printing caught without executing throw/catch would not demonstrate exception support.

If an older browser reports a provider limitation, that is not a learner error on the throw line. Do not rewrite exceptions as return codes to claim this outcome. A compatible browser update and a separate native run provide different evidence. Offline compilation must first be prepared through the normal flow; an available lesson text alone does not ensure it.

sections.title: Laboratory and cumulative practice
paragraphs: Save both laboratory runs: successful replacement and failure before commit. Record state before and after, plus resource counts. Explain why moving throw after swap would destroy the strong guarantee even if no resource leaked. This is a safe reasoning counterexample; the working implementation should retain its original promise.

The cumulative practicum combines a virtual strategy with an exception for an invalid argument. After rejection, saved remains seven. Add your own preservation check and explain the caller's policy. Templates come next. They do not have exceptions as a hard prerequisite, although they follow them in the module's teaching sequence.

selfcheck.feedback: Transfer to a matching handler unwinds the exited scope and destroys the fully constructed Guard. Its destructor releases the resource before catch; the handler does not automatically delete arbitrary addresses.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the strong guarantee promise?
options: No change to specified state on failure.
Every external effect is rolled back.
selfcheck.feedback: The strong guarantee concerns specified observable state at the operation boundary. The call may throw, but failure preserves that state; already performed external effects are not automatically undone.

selfcheck.prompt: Does a bare throw; preserve dynamic type?
options: No; the type always becomes int.
Yes; it propagates the current exception.
selfcheck.feedback: A bare throw propagates the current exception without creating a new base copy. throw e can copy the static base portion and therefore lose the derived exception type.

selfcheck.prompt: Does native execution prove browser EH?
options: No; separate real browser execution is required.
selfcheck.feedback: Native and browser runtimes use different compilers, ABIs and execution mechanisms. Browser EH requires a real throw/catch through its Worker, not a native success or a preprinted word.

selfcheck.prompt: Does swap undo an already sent message?
options: Yes; swap rolls back the world.
No; external effects have a separate contract.
Yes; if the vector is empty.
selfcheck.feedback: swap exchanges the specified objects' state but cannot retract a message or write already performed. Separate such effects from prepare/commit or give them their own recovery protocol.

practice.title: Laboratory: Exceptions and error guarantees
practice.task: Read mode=0…1. Store starts with {1,2}; replace prepares a copy with nine appended and throws runtime_error before swap when mode is one. Guard tracks a resource. After the attempt print ok or rejected, current Store sum and active. Invalid input: invalid. Zero gives ok 12 0; one gives rejected 3 0.
criteria: active is already zero in the handler.
Name the observable boundary of each.
Sums are twelve and three, with active zero in both.
The strong guarantee would fail even without a leak.
Include source, actual results, an independent case and limits of the conclusion.

terms.definition: Transfer of control with an error object to a matching handler.
An expression initiating an exceptional path or rethrowing an exception.
An exception handler selected by type-matching rules.
Cleanup of constructed automatic objects in exited scopes.
Preservation of invariants without resource leaks after failure.
No observable change to the specified state after failure.
The final step publishing prepared replacement state.
A bare throw; propagates the current exception and preserves its type.
